body:
Full-codebase review, Android finding. Verified by reading SyncEngine.kt.

On `410 full_resync_required` the engine calls `appDb.clearAllTables()`, justified by "nothing pushed is lost". That holds only for the rows in THIS batch: the push is capped at 250 rows (`take(MAX_CHANGES_PER_SYNC)`), and quarantined rows are excluded from `dirtyRows()` entirely. Everything beyond the cap, and every row the user has not yet fixed after a refusal, is destroyed without a word.

Scenario: a week offline, 400 edits, the account's cursor has fallen below the server's gc_horizon. The first sync pushes 250, gets 410, wipes the database — the other 150 edits are gone.

Fix direction: drain the whole backlog before honouring the 410, or snapshot dirty and blocked rows and re-insert them after the cursor-0 pull. Test gap: the existing 410 test uses exactly one dirty row, i.e. the case where nothing can be lost.
title: Android: a full resync wipes offline edits beyond the pushed batch and every quarantined row
